items.title: Targeting MCT1 suppresses humoral response and autoimmunity via the NAD(H) redox state.
items.authors: Shu-Li Wei, Ying Yang, Cong-Cong Wang, Xue-Min Li, Yuan-Wei Li, Xiao-Li Li
items.abstract: Immunometabolism has garnered significant attention due to its essential roles in regulating B cell activation, proliferation and differentiation. Monocarboxylate transporters (MCTs), a family of solute carrier transporters responsible for lactate transport across biological membranes, have been shown to play a pivotal role in immune responses across various immune cell types. However, the expression and functional significance of MCTs in B cells remain poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrated that germinal center B cells and activated B cells exhibit elevated levels of MCT1 expression. Pharmacologically blocking MCT1 with AZD3965 inhibited both T-cell dependent and independent humoral response and ameliorated autoimmunity in the experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis. Mechanically, MCT1 blockade led to the accumulation of intracellular lactate, which in turn suppressed NAD + regeneration, thereby inhibiting B cell activation and survival. Taken together, these findings suggest that MCT1 might be a potential therapeutical target in antibody-mediate autoimmune disease.
items.zhSummary: 本研究探讨了单羧酸转运蛋白1（MCT1）在B细胞中的表达及其功能意义。研究发现生发中心B细胞和活化B细胞中MCT1表达升高。使用MCT1抑制剂AZD3965后，T细胞依赖和非依赖的体液免疫反应均受抑制，且在实验性自身免疫性重症肌无力模型中自身免疫症状改善。机制方面，MCT1阻断导致胞内乳酸积累，抑制NAD+再生，进而抑制B细胞活化和存活。研究基于实验模型，具体临床效果及安全性未涉及。

items.title: Effectiveness of Thymectomy in Alleviating Myasthenia Gravis Symptoms: A Two-Decade Multicenter Experience from Pakistan.
items.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
items.authors: Muhammad S Nabi, Muhammad Naeem, Zeeshan Sarwar, Rafay Shamshad, Hassan Iftikhar
items.abstract: Thymectomy is an established therapeutic option for myasthenia gravis (MG), but long-term outcomes and predictors of remission from low- and middle-income countries remain limited. This study reports a 20-year, two-center experience evaluating surgical outcomes, neurological improvement, and prognostic factors following thymectomy. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 455 patients with MG who underwent thymectomy between January 2005 and December 2024 at two tertiary centers in Lahore, Pakistan. Neurological outcomes were assessed using the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America Post-Intervention Status. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of favorable outcomes, defined as complete stable remission (CSR) or pharmacologic remission. The mean age was 36.8 ± 13.1 years, with a female predominance (62.4%). Transsternal thymectomy was performed in 63.1% of patients and video-assisted thoracoscopic in 36.9%. Thymic hyperplasia was the most common pathology (55.2%), followed by thymoma (37.8%). At a mean follow-up of 74 ± 38 months, symptomatic improvement was achieved in 85.3% of patients. CSR and pharmacologic remission were observed in 31.2% and 24.6% of patients, respectively. Medication requirements declined significantly postoperatively ( P < 0.001). Five-year recurrence-free survival was 93.2%, and overall survival was 96.4%. Multivariate analysis identified shorter disease duration (<24 months) and non-thymomatous pathology as independent predictors of favorable neurological outcomes. Thymectomy was associated with durable neurological improvement and a significant reduction in medication dependence among patients with MG. Early surgical intervention, particularly in patients with non-thymomatous disease, was associated with better long-term outcomes, while minimally invasive approaches offered comparable efficacy with reduced perioperative morbidity.
items.zhSummary: 本研究回顾性分析了2005年至2024年期间巴基斯坦两中心455例重症肌无力患者行胸腺切除术的长期疗效及预后因素。患者平均年龄36.8岁，女性居多。随访平均74个月，85.3%患者症状改善，完全稳定缓解率31.2%，药物缓解率24.6%，药物依赖显著下降。术后五年无复发生存率为93.2%。短病程(<24个月)和非胸腺瘤病理为预后良好独立预测因素。微创胸腺切除术与传统术式疗效相当且围手术期并发症较少。

items.title: Comprehensive metabolomic characterization of patients with myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Xiaowen Yang, Jing Qin, Jing Liu, Tianlong Liu
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is mediated by abnormal antibody generation and is characterized by muscle weakness and pathological fatigue. However, the accuracy of anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody testing for the diagnosis of MG needs improvement. This study was aimed to systematically characterize the plasma metabolome of patients with MG and identify novel biomarkers with significant diagnostic value. A cohort of 130 subjects was enrolled and divided into discovery and validation sets, and their plasma metabolomic profiles were determined by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Metabolomic variables were analyzed along with clinical information to identify relevant diagnostic biomarkers. The diagnostic efficacy of the screened metabolites and biomarker panel was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. In positive and negative ion modes, plasma metabolomic profiling revealed 326 and 398 differentially abundant metabolites, respectively, in the discovery and validation sets. The metabolomic profile distinguished patients with MG from healthy controls across the two cohorts evaluated in this study. Furthermore, 890 metabolites were detected in both the discovery and validation sets. Metabolite set enrichment analysis of these 890 metabolites revealed that steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway was significantly enriched, implying that altered metabolism may serve as a potential pathological hallmark of MG. On the basis of the differences between groups, compound level, the value of the variable importance in projection, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and precision-recall curve analyses, 3 differentially abundant metabolites, namely, LysoPE(P-18:1/0:0), PE(O-18:1/0:0) and PE(P-16:0/0:0), were selected as a biomarker panel to distinguish between patients with MG and healthy controls. ROC curve (AUC) analysis revealed that the biomarker panel and anti-AChR antibody testing had equivalent MG diagnostic ability (AUC: 0.883 vs. 0.825; P = 0.058 in the discovery set; AUC: 0.843 vs. 0.722; P = 0.121 in the validation set); moreover, the combination of the biomarker panel and anti-AChR antibody testing significantly improved the clinical diagnosis of MG in the discovery and validation sets compared with anti-AChR antibody testing alone. Our screened biomarker panel discriminated patients with established MG from healthy healthy controls, however, further evaluation in independent cohorts including patients with suspected MG and other relevant autoimmune and neuromuscular junction disease healthy controls is warranted.
items.zhSummary: 本研究系统性分析了重症肌无力（MG）患者的血浆代谢组，旨在发现具有诊断价值的新型生物标志物。研究纳入130名受试者，分为发现组和验证组，采用液相色谱-串联质谱技术检测代谢物。结果显示发现与验证组分别有326和398种差异代谢物，且两组均能区分MG患者与健康对照。890种代谢物参与的甾体激素生物合成通路被显著富集。筛选出LysoPE(P-18:1/0:0)、PE(O-18:1/0:0)和PE(P-16:0/0:0)三种代谢物组成生物标志物组合，诊断效能与抗乙酰胆碱受体抗体检测相当，且联合使用诊断价值提升。研究建议进一步在疑似MG及其他神经免疫疾病队列中验证。研究局限包括缺乏独立队列的外部验证及对其他相关疾病的鉴别能力尚不明确。

items.title: Anesthetic Management of a Patient With Myasthenia Gravis Undergoing Thoracoscopic Thymectomy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.authors: Rufaidah Alchuban, Abdulrahman AlSulaiti, Khadija Abuhassan, Vishal Shah
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness and fatigability. Perioperative management is challenging because patients may have bulbar or respiratory muscle involvement and altered sensitivity to neuromuscular blocking agents, increasing the risk of postoperative respiratory failure and myasthenic crisis. Thymectomy is an established therapeutic option in selected patients with myasthenia gravis and may be performed using minimally invasive thoracoscopic techniques. We report the anesthetic management of a 48-year-old man with generalized acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MGFA class IIb) scheduled for thoracoscopic thymectomy. The patient had a recent relapse with diplopia, dysphagia, and easy fatigability, which improved after medical therapy. Preoperative optimization included intravenous immunoglobulin therapy for four days. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and remifentanil without initial neuromuscular blockade. Tracheal intubation was facilitated using video laryngoscopy after topical lidocaine. Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane, and invasive monitoring was established. Because of the surgical requirement for improved thoracoscopic visualization, a reduced dose of rocuronium was administered intraoperatively under train-of-four monitoring. At the end of surgery, neuromuscular blockade was reversed with sugammadex, and the patient was successfully extubated and transferred to the intensive care unit in stable condition. This case highlights the importance of careful preoperative optimization, avoidance of neuromuscular blocking agents when possible, quantitative neuromuscular monitoring, and individualized use of low-dose rocuronium with sugammadex reversal when muscle relaxation is required during thoracoscopic thymectomy in patients with myasthenia gravis.
items.zhSummary: 本病例报告描述了一例48岁AChR抗体阳性重症肌无力（MGFA IIb级）患者行胸腔镜胸腺切除术的麻醉管理。患者术前经免疫球蛋白治疗优化，麻醉诱导避免使用神经肌肉阻滞剂，手术中在神经肌肉功能监测下少量应用罗库溴铵并最终用舒更葡糖钠拮抗，术后顺利拔管转入ICU。提示术前充分优化、神经肌肉阻滞剂谨慎使用及肌松监测对MG胸腺切除术麻醉管理的重要性。

items.title: Disease Control in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: Consensus Definition, Evolution, and Patient Characterization.
items.authors: David Reyes-Leiva, Álvaro Carbayo, Ana Vesperinas, Fernando Caballero-Martínez, Ricardo Rojas-Garcia, Janina Turon-Sans
items.abstract: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a chronic fluctuating neuromuscular disease. Some patients keep experiencing symptoms or adverse events (AEs) despite tailored therapeutic schemes. The aim of this study was to characterize adequately controlled gMG and describe patients' evolution and outcomes, including estimated direct health costs in a universal health care system. Spanish expert neurologists developed a definition of adequately controlled gMG using Delphi methodology. This was applied to an existing cohort of patients recently diagnosed with gMG during 1998-2020 in a Spanish referral neuromuscular diseases' unit. Control status, clinical outcomes, AEs, and health care resource utilization (HCRU) were described biennially. We assessed 220 patients diagnosed with gMG (54.5% women; mean age at onset of 58 years; 84% anti-AChR, 6% anti-MuSK, 10% seronegative). Adequately controlled gMG was defined as achieving Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America Post-Intervention Status classification of clinical stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or minimal manifestations stable for a year; having an MG-ADL score ≤2; experiencing no clinical exacerbations during the last year requiring a change in immunosuppressive therapy or rescue therapy; and having no or mild AE to therapies (100% of experts in agreement or total agreement). The proportion adequately controlled (AC) patients increased from 62.0% at 2 years after first visit to 81.9% after 8 years of follow-up. 47.3% of patients remained AC in every observation, and 17.7% remained not adequately controlled (NC) in every observation. No features were significantly associated with adequate control. AE-related drug interruption rates were higher in NC patients (ranging from 50% to 100% during the study). The mean cost per patient/year ranged from 2,718.6€ in the first biennial period to 843.1€ in the last biennial period for AC patients and from 10,190.1€ to 5,827.4€ for NC patients. Based on the new gMG control consensus definition, almost 1 in 5 patients do not reach disease control even after 8 years of evolution. Those patients lacked specific clinical features, underscoring the unpredictability of the gMG course. Burden of AE-related drug interruptions, HCRU, and costs per patients/year were higher among those patients NC. However, our study is unicentric and included patients from a referral unit, with a possible overrepresentation of NC patients.
items.zhSummary: 本研究通过Delphi方法制定了广泛性重症肌无力(gMG)的病情充分控制定义，并应用于1998-2020年西班牙神经肌肉病转诊中心诊治的220例gMG患者队列。定义包括临床稳定缓解、MG-ADL评分≤2、无需治疗调整的临床加重、及无或轻度药物不良事件。随访观察中，充分控制患者比例由2年时62.0%增至8年后81.9%。约47.3%患者持续充分控制，17.7%患者始终未能控制。未发现显著预测充分控制的临床特征。未充分控制患者的不良事件导致药物停药率较高，医疗资源使用和直接费用也明显增加。研究局限于单中心且患者可能存在未充分控制者的选择偏倚。

items.title: Serum utrophin levels in patients with myasthenia gravis: an exploratory study.
items.authors: Manato Yasuda, Akiyuki Uzawa, Etsuko Ogaya, Hideo Handa, Kentaro Kurumada, Hiroyuki Akamine
items.abstract: The role of utrophin, a protein expressed at neuromuscular junctions, remains unclear in myasthenia gravis (MG). This study aimed to investigate serum utrophin levels in immunotherapy-naïve patients with different MG subtypes and evaluate changes before and after immunotherapy initiation. We measured serum utrophin levels in immunotherapy-naïve MG patients ( n = 39), including acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive MG (AChR-MG) ( n = 30; ocular type: n = 10, generalized type: n = 20) and muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibody-positive MG (MuSK-MG) ( n = 9; all generalized type) patients and healthy controls (HCs) ( n = 21). We analyzed relationships between serum utrophin levels, clinical parameters, and antibody levels. In generalized AChR-MG, serum utrophin levels were measured before and after immunotherapy. Median serum utrophin levels tended to be higher in patients with MG than in HCs (34.0 vs. 13.8 ng/mL; Hodges-Lehmann estimate, 7.04 ng/mL; 95% confidence interval: -0.09-37.3; p = 0.051). In MuSK-MG, an exploratory positive correlation with the MG Foundation of America (MGFA) classification was observed (ρ = 0.69, nominal p = 0.041). In generalized AChR-MG, median concentrations numerically decreased from 43.8 to 20.2 ng/mL after immunotherapy ( p = 0.064), but no significant change was observed in the 15 patients whose paired samples were both within the standard range ( p = 0.80). These exploratory findings suggest that circulating utrophin may reflect disease-related biological changes in MG, although definitive conclusions regarding its biomarker utility cannot be drawn. Further validation in larger cohorts using analytically validated assays is warranted.
items.zhSummary: 本研究探索性检测了免疫治疗初治的重症肌无力（MG）患者血清中utrophin水平，涵盖AChR抗体阳性和MuSK抗体阳性MG不同亚型。结果显示MG患者血清utrophin水平较健康对照有上升趋势，MuSK-MG的utrophin水平与MGFA分级呈正相关。广泛型AChR-MG患者接受免疫治疗后utrophin水平呈下降趋势，但部分病例变化不显著。研究提示utrophin可能反映MG相关的生物学变化，但尚难确立其生物标志物价值，需更大样本和经过验证的检测方法进一步确认。

items.title: Rapid Serum IgG Reduction as a Potential Indicator of Short-Term Clinical Improvement in AChR-Ab-Positive Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: A Post Hoc Analysis of a Phase III Batoclimab Trial.
items.authors: Jianying Xi, Yaoxian Yue, Yuzhou Guan, Ruisheng Duan, Qun Xue, Haishan Jiang
items.abstract: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is an autoimmune disorder often associated with anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Abs). Identifying short-term predictors or indicators of clinical improvement is crucial for optimizing treatment strategies. This post hoc analysis utilized data from a phase III, multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolling 65 patients with AChR-Ab-positive gMG across 27 centers in China. We evaluated serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) as a potential short-term indicator of clinical improvement in patients treated with batoclimab. Clinical severity was evaluated using the Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) and Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) scales. Spearman correlation analyses, mixed-effects models, and multivariate analyses were performed to assess relations between biomarker changes and symptom improvement. Within-patient Spearman correlation showed significant associations between reductions in IgG or AChR-Ab levels and symptom improvement (ΔIgG vs. MG-ADL change: r = 0.372, p < 0.001; ΔIgG vs. QMG change: r = 0.492, p < 0.001). Mixed-effects modeling indicated that an 80% reduction in IgG corresponded to a 59% probability of MG-ADL improvement by ≥ 3 points and a 77% probability of QMG improvement by ≥ 3 points. High baseline body mass index (BMI) was identified as an independent risk factor for slower IgG decline. Batoclimab rapidly reduced IgG and pathogenic AChR-Ab levels, leading to improved clinical outcomes in patients with gMG. items.title: Explainable Machine Learning Model for Personalized Assessment of the Need for Intensive Care in Patients with Myasthenia Gravis Based on Phenotype and Inflammatory Markers.
items.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
items.authors: Che-Cheng Chang, Kuan-Yu Lin, Jiann-Horng Yeh, Hou-Chang Chiu, Tzu-Chi Liu, Chi-Jie Lu
items.abstract: Early identification of myasthenia gravis (MG) severe exacerbations that require intensive care unit (ICU) admission remains challenging due disease highly heterogeneous. Existing models seldom incorporate phenotype stratification, limiting interpretability and clinical utility. This study aimed to develop an explainable machine learning (ML) model to assess phenotype-specific risk factors and predict ICU admission for patients with MG. This retrospective study included 319 hospitalized patients with MG. We utilized clinical variables and systemic inflammation markers for ML modeling. Subgroups were prespecified by thymoma status and age at onset. Primary outcome was need for intensive care during the hospitalization. Model performance was assessed. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed for interpretation of global and individual features. Of 319 admissions, 33 (10.3%) required ICU care. Four ML models were trained with nested 3-fold validation. eXtreme Gradient Boosting performed best (AUC: 0.94). SHAP ranked MGFA clinical classification, infection during admission, body mass index, and inflammatory indices as principal predictors. Subgroup analyses revealed phenotype-specific patterns, including opposite SHAP directions for inflammatory markers between thymoma and non-thymoma groups and distinct rankings between different age of onset groups. SHAP-based personalized explanations revealed patient-specific variations in risk ranking and directionality of predictive features. A web-based calculator was developed to support real-time clinical implementation of the model, potentially allowing for risk stratification. An explainable machine learning framework that integrates clinical features with systemic inflammation indices reliably predicts ICU admission in MG and reveals phenotype-specific risk patterns, enabling personalized risk stratification in MG management.

items.title: The Expanding Therapeutic Landscape in Myasthenia Gravis.
items.authors: Hebatallah R Rashed
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a rare autoimmune disorder caused by autoantibodies targeting postsynaptic proteins of the neuromuscular junction. Although conventional therapies can achieve remission or sufficient symptom control in most patients with generalized MG (gMG), approximately 10%-30% of patients remain treatment refractory with an increased risk of myasthenic crises and mortality. In addition, prolonged immunosuppression can cause undesirable side effects. Over the past decade, research has focused on identifying new therapeutic targets, which paved the way to advance the development of novel therapies. Rather than exerting broad immunosuppression, novel therapies selectively target specific components involved in the immunopathogenesis of MG, such as immunoglobulin G (IgG) production (B cell-depleting agents), IgG recycling (neonatal fragment crystallizable receptor, FcRn, blocker), and complement activation (complement inhibitors). Targeted therapies have been evolving exponentially since 2017, marking a new era in treatment strategies in gMG. They have emerged as potential steroid-sparing agents with robust efficacy and favorable safety profiles. Small cohorts have demonstrated the efficacy and tolerability of these therapies during myasthenic crisis and in patients with active thymoma. Although targeted therapies have generally comparable efficacy and safety, treatment plans should be individualized, and several factors should be considered before initiating these therapies, including pharmacological spectrum (complement inhibitors are effective only in acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG, while FcRn and B cell-depleting agents have broader spectra), convenience of administration, and cost-effectiveness. This monograph proposes an updated treatment algorithm in refractory gMG that integrates novel targeted therapies alongside standard immunosuppressant steroid-sparing agents.

items.title: A potential biomarker for the efficacy of complement inhibitors in myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Etsuko Ogaya, Akiyuki Uzawa, Hiroyuki Akamine, Manato Yasuda, Hideo Handa, Kentaro Kurumada
items.abstract: In acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MG), complement activation is a major mechanism underlying impaired neuromuscular transmission and complement inhibitors are used in clinical practice. In the absence of biomarkers predicting responsiveness to complement inhibitors, this study aimed to identify novel predictors. Serum samples from 14 patients with AChR antibody-positive MG and 10 healthy controls (HCs) were incubated with AChR-expressing HEK293 cells. AChR binding IgG and membrane attack complex (MAC) deposition were quantified by flow cytometry. The correlations of these indices with clinical manifestations were analyzed. Patients with MG showed higher mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) than HCs for AChR-bound IgG (median: 4614 vs 172; 95% CI 1588-7451, P < 0.001) and MAC deposition (488 vs 227; 95% CI 59-495, P < 0.001). The MFI of AChR-bound IgG correlated with baseline MG Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) scores (Spearman r s = 0.58; 95% CI 0.05-0.85, P = 0.033). Improvement in MG-ADL scores correlated with the MFI of AChR-bound IgG, MAC deposition, and the proportion of AChR-bound IgG + /MAC deposition + double-positive cells. Responders to complement inhibitors had higher proportions of double-positive cells than non-responders (median: 74% vs 0.2%; 95% CI 15-94, P = 0.022). The MFI values of AChR-bound IgG correlated with disease severity, and the proportion of double-positive cells may represent a potential biomarker of therapeutic response to complement inhibition. Prospective validation is needed to assess its predictive value.

items.title: Case Report: Efgartigimod in refractory non-tumor Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.
items.authors: Ana Baltasar-Corral, Nuria García-Barragán, Beatriz Zarza-Sanz, Francisco Javier Buisán-Catevilla, Beatriz Montero-Llorente, Miguel Angel Rodríguez-Sagrado
items.abstract: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) is a rare autoimmune disorder, associated with neoplastic disease in 50-60% of cases. In severe cases, currently available immunomodulatory therapies frequently fail to achieve adequate control. We report a 20-year-old woman with non-tumor LEMS refractory to 3,4-diaminopyridine, sequential immunosuppression with prednisone, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil and rituximab and plasma exchange, who remained severely disabled after two years of progressive disease. Off-label efgartigimod (1000mg subcutaneously weekly for four weeks, with the interval between cycles initially adjusted according to symptom recurrence), produced rapid and sustained clinical improvement, including recovery from a respiratory decompensation episode. The Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) score decreased from a baseline of 5-9 to a minimum of 2, and the Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score improved from 13-18 to 8-11. Symptoms consistently recurred toward the end of the third week of each treatment-free interval, prompting a fixed two-week interval, which stabilized clinical response and reduced fluctuation severity. This is, to our knowledge, the first report of sustained clinical benefit from FcRn inhibition in non-paraneoplastic, long-standing refractory LEMS. As in myasthenia gravis, LEMS is mediated by pathogenic circulating IgG antibodies, and these findings support FcRn inhibition as a rational treatment strategy in refractory LEMS regardless of tumor association.

items.title: The Efficacy and Safety of Tocilizumab in the Treatment of Refractory Ocular Myasthenia Gravis in Pediatric Patients.
items.authors: Qing-Qing Wang, Xiang-Qi Cao, Bi-Ying Zhang, Xiao-Xi Huang, Si-Jia Hao, Ting Chang
items.abstract: Refractory pediatric ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) remains difficult to manage. We evaluated tocilizumab's efficacy and safety in these patients. In this single-center, retrospective analysis of prospectively collected registry data from Tangdu Hospital (China), pediatric refractory OMG patients received intravenous tocilizumab (8 mg/kg every 4 weeks) for 16 weeks as add-on therapy. Refractory disease required persistent symptoms despite adequate trials of ≥ 2 immunosuppressants, frequent relapses during glucocorticoid tapering, or intolerance of conventional oral immunosuppressants. The primary outcome was change in Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) score from baseline to Weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16, analyzed using generalized estimating equations. All 10 patients (1 male, 9 females; median age 5.5 years, range 2-11) completed 16 weeks of follow-up. Seven (70%) were positive for antiacetylcholine receptor antibody (AChR-Ab). At Week 4, mean MG-ADL score decreased from 3.4 to 2.5 (incidence rate ratio[IRR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.54-0.99; p = 0.048), with further reduction to 1.5 at week 16 (IRR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.24-0.80; p = 0.007). Similarly, mean Quantitative MG (QMG) score dropped from 4.7 at baseline to 3.0 at Week 4 (IRR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.41-0.99; p = 0.048) and further to 1.9 at Week 16 (IRR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.24-0.69; p = 0.001). By Week 16, 50% of patients achieved minimal symptom expression, and 50% reduced prednisone requirements. Tocilizumab was well-tolerated with only one transient infusion-related dizziness. These preliminary findings suggest that tocilizumab may offer a safe and effective treatment option for children with refractory OMG.

items.title: The Duke Myasthenia Gravis Clinic Registry: IV. Does Race Affect the Outcome of Treatment of Myasthenia Gravis? A Single Center Retrospective Analysis.
items.authors: Mao Liu, Chunlu Ma, Michael W Lutz, Vern C Juel, Janice M Massey, Lisa D Hobson-Webb
items.abstract: Few studies have investigated the role of race in the long-term outcome of patients with myasthenia gravis (MG). The aim of this study is to analyze clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes related to race in patients with MG. This is a retrospective review of data from patients seen between 1980 and 2016 and followed for at least 2 years in the Duke MG Clinic. Treatment goal (TG) was defined as achieving MGFA postintervention status of "minimal manifestations" or better. Multivariable logistic regression analysis and Cox proportional hazards (CPH) modeling were performed to assess the effect of race on TG by adjusting for other variables. Among 820 patients (661 White, 81%; 159 Black, 19%), Black patients had a younger median age at disease onset, female predominance, higher rate of muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies and thymectomy, and less non-corticosteroid immunosuppressant use. The percentage of White patients in the Registry is greater than the mean in the North Carolina census between 1980 and 2010 (81% vs. 77%, p = 0.014). Disease duration and MGFA class at first visit, thymectomy, follow-up duration, median time to TG, TG achievement and maintenance, median time to TG loss, and corticosteroid/PLEX/IVIG use were similar in the two racial groups. Neither multivariable logistic regression nor CPH modeling identified race as an independent predictor of TG. Although racial differences were observed in patients with MG, long-term outcomes were similar in Black and White patients. Our study suggests that following treatment guidelines is important in achieving favorable MG outcomes.

items.title: Novel compounds induce AChR clustering and improve motor function in myasthenia gravis animal models.
items.authors: Asako Saito, Ryuichi Sekioka, Akira Nagashima, Takuya Washio, Eriko Honjo, Yohei Koganemaru
items.abstract: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the synapse between motor nerves and skeletal muscles, is implicated in the pathogenesis of various neuromuscular disorders, including myasthenia gravis (MG), congenital myasthenia, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Postsynaptic clustering of acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) is crucial for NMJ formation. This process is initiated by agrin, a glycoprotein secreted from motor nerve terminals, which activates muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) via its coreceptor, low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 4 (Lrp4), and thereby activates downstream signaling pathways that induce AChR clustering. MG is an autoimmune disease characterized by the production of autoantibodies against NMJ components such as AChR, MuSK, and Lrp4, which leads to impaired neuromuscular transmission and motor dysfunction. In this study, we identified orally active small-molecule compounds that promote AChR clustering through the Lrp4-MuSK signaling axis. Knockdown experiments demonstrated that Lrp4 was responsible for the compounds to induce AChR clustering. The compounds induced MuSK phosphorylation following the compound treatment in C2C12 cells and improved motor function and increased muscle volume in both MuSK-MG mice and AChR-MG rat models. Together, these findings identify orally active small molecules that potentiate Lrp4-MuSK signaling and highlight a pharmacological strategy to modulate NMJ function for MG and related neuromuscular disorders.

items.title: Patient engagement in protocol development for rare disease clinical trials: a framework.
items.authors: Janella Beltran, Sarah Bolton, Pesh Patel, Rohita Sharma
items.abstract: Meaningful patient engagement requires understanding lived disease and healthcare experiences. This patient-centric approach is especially valuable when applied to the design and execution of clinical trials, as participation barriers may hinder trial recruitment, retention, and detection of meaningful outcomes. Patient engagement is particularly important in the study of treatments for rare diseases, where populations are small and geographically dispersed and there are few sites with relevant clinical expertise. Additionally, protocol amendments to address hurdles are expensive and can cause delays in trial activities, which can affect downstream regulatory approvals and access to treatments. Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, worked with patients and their stakeholders to identify points of additional trial burden and enable patient-driven changes before clinical trial protocol finalization. Patients, parents of pediatric patients, and patient advocacy group representatives with diverse experiences participated in virtual, study-specific perspective exchange sessions on 4 protocols (adults with generalized myasthenia gravis, pediatric patients with generalized myasthenia gravis, adults with antibody-mediated rejection after kidney transplantation, and adults with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy). Participants discussed their disease journey, the protocol, and perceived barriers to clinical trial awareness, enrollment, participation, and follow-up through semistructured interviews. Participants raised points about the eligibility criteria, study drug self-administration, visit frequency, participant mental health, and the relevance of specific outcome measures. In response, the study sponsor proactively changed the clinical trial protocols when feasible. Changes included expanding the eligibility criteria, developing an instructional video on self-administration of the study drug, and reducing the frequency of clinic visits. In addition, the sponsor created appreciation cards and trained trial sites on a standardized approach to help participants understand the goals of specific outcome measures. These insights led to demonstrable, advocate-recommended changes in rare disease clinical trial protocols before study delivery, underscoring how early patient-partnered drug development can be meaningfully applied to research in rare diseases. NCT05556096, NCT06607627, NCT06744647, and NCT06183931. Not applicable. Running clinical trials in rare diseases can be difficult for a number of reasons: (1) recruiting patients can be a challenge because there are so few people with any one rare disease; (2) there isn’t much information about which study goals will make a difference for patients; and (3) patients often drop out of trials, which take a lot of time and effort. When changes are needed to address these challenges, researchers have to change the design of the trial after it has started. This is time consuming, expensive, and can delay treatment approval and patient access. The goal of this initiative was to show that if patients were involved in trial design prior to study initiation, the study organizer would be able to address potential issues before the trial started. Patients and their caregivers provided input into the design of 4 trials during virtual meetings with researchers. Participants talked about what parts of the trial would make it hard for people to participate and whether they thought the trial was answering the right questions. For example, participants raised concerns about how often they would have to go for trial visits. The researchers then made changes to the trial protocols based on the feedback gathered. These patient-guided changes improved the trial design before it started. By working with patients, researchers were able to make the trials more patient friendly. The initiative found that including patient perspective was truly beneficial in the design of clinical trials.

items.title: Safety of Ravulizumab Use in Pregnancy: Insights from a Global Pharmacovigilance Analysis.
items.authors: Cynthia Carrillo Infante, Arshad Mujeebuddin, Meghana Koneru, Cory Williams
items.abstract: Ravulizumab, a second-generation terminal complement C5 inhibitor (engineered from eculizumab) is approved for the treatment of rare complement-mediated disorders paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD). While eculizumab has an established pregnancy safety profile across these indications, data on ravulizumab during pregnancy and lactation remain limited. This analysis evaluated pregnancy-related safety and outcomes following ravulizumab exposure using global post-marketing data. All globally reported pregnancy cases with ≥ 1 documented ravulizumab dose were identified from the Alexion pharmacovigilance database (December 21, 2018 through December 31, 2025). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient demographics, treatment patterns, and pregnancy outcomes. The 354 pregnancy cases with ≥ 1 dose of ravulizumab exposure that were identified include all reported cases: PNH (n = 160), aHUS (n = 72), no condition reported (n = 45), gMG (n = 38), NMOSD (n = 34), and other (n = 5). Among cases with pregnancy outcome data (n = 106), the ravulizumab exposure included full-pregnancy exposure (17.0%), ravulizumab-to-eculizumab switch during pregnancy (24.5%), and incomplete exposure details reported (58.5%). Pregnancy outcomes included 68 live births (64.2%), 29 spontaneous abortions (27.4%), 3 fetal deaths (2.8%), and 6 elective terminations (5.7%). For a nested subset of 44 post-marketing cases with detailed ravulizumab exposure data, as well as information on pregnancy outcomes (PNH [n = 26], aHUS [n = 10], gMG [n = 3], NMOSD [n = 3], and not reported [n = 2]), live births were reported in 32 cases (72.7%), spontaneous abortions in 11 cases (25.0%), and elective terminations in 1 case (2.3%). This post-marketing analysis provides real-world insights on ravulizumab exposure during pregnancy and suggests favorable outcomes and no unexpected safety signals similar to eculizumab. The findings may support shared decision-making between prescribers and patients when considering the ravulizumab use during pregnancy. An ongoing global observational ravulizumab pregnancy study will further inform the safety profile (NCT06312644).

items.title: Association Between Pleural Breach and Perioperative and Long-Term Outcomes after Thymectomy for Myasthenia Gravis: A Two-Center Retrospective Study.
items.authors: Muhammad Shoaib Nabi, Zeeshan Sarwar, Rafay Shamshad, Hassan Iftikhar
items.abstract: Thymectomy is an established treatment for myasthenia gravis and thymic tumors. This study evaluated the impact of pleural breach on perioperative pleural-related morbidity and long-term neurologic and oncologic outcomes following thymectomy. A retrospective multicenter review of 455 patients who underwent thymectomy between January 2005 and December 2024 was conducted at Services Hospital and Surgimed Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan. Patients underwent either a partial transsternal thymectomy (n = 273) or a video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) thymectomy (n = 182). The primary outcome was pleural-related postoperative morbidity. Secondary outcomes included neurologic remission, recurrence-free survival (RFS), postoperative complications, and hospital stay. Pleural breach occurred in all VATS cases and incidentally in 29 (10.6%) transsternal cases. VATS thymectomy was associated with lower blood loss ( P < 0.001) and shorter hospital stay ( P < 0.001), but with longer operative time ( P < 0.001). Pleural-related complications were more frequent following pleural breach, but were generally transient and were managed conservatively. On multivariable analysis, pleural breach independently predicted pleural-related morbidity [odds ratio (OR): 2.6, P = 0.006]. The combined proportion of patients achieving complete stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or clinical improvement exceeded 90%. Neurologic remission and 5-year RFS were comparable between groups ( P = 0.612 and P = 0.538, respectively). Pleural breach during thymectomy was independently associated with increased transient pleural-related postoperative morbidity (OR: 2.6). However, these complications were generally self-limited and managed conservatively. Long-term neurologic remission and RFS were comparable between surgical approaches, but these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective observational design.

items.title: Clinical outcomes during pregnancy and the postpartum period in women with myasthenia gravis and their newborns.
items.authors: Amanda Vitória Freire de Oliveira, Ana Flávia Andrade Lemos, Mariana Ribeiro Pereira, Rodrigo Siqueira Soares Frezatti, André Cleriston José Dos Santos, Claudia Ferreira da Rosa Sobreira
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disease of the neuromuscular junction associated with increased maternal and fetal risks during pregnancy and the puerperal period. To describe the longitudinal course of MG, maternal and neonatal outcomes, and the occurrence of transient neonatal myasthenia gravis (TNMG) from the pregestational period until 12 months postpartum in pregnancies complicated by MG. A retrospective, longitudinal case-series study of pregnancies in women with MG who were followed at a single tertiary center for neuromuscular disorders. Disease severity was assessed using the MG Foundation of America Clinical Classification (MGFA)and MG-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) scale. Treatments, delivery mode, postpartum exacerbations, ventilatory support and TNMG in newborns were collected using a standardized proforma. Longitudinal MG-ADL scores were analyzed using generalized estimating equations. Twenty-four pregnant women with MG were included. Patients had juvenile-onset ( n = 12, 50%) or early-onset ( n = 12, 50%) MG, which was mostly generalized ( n = 20, 83%). Anti-AChR antibodies were positive in 71% ( n = 17) and anti-MuSK antibodies in 4% ( n = 1). Pyridostigmine was the main therapy; 8% of patients ( n = 2) experienced exacerbations during pregnancy. Cesarean delivery occurred in 60% ( n = 12), primarily for obstetric indications. The TNMG occurred in 15% of newborns (3 out of 20), and all fully recovered. The MG-ADL scores increased during the first and third trimesters, during the postpartum period, and at 12 months postpartum. Third-trimester MG-ADL scores ≥ 4 were associated with the occurrence of TNMG. No maternal or neonatal deaths occurred. Pregnancy in MG was characterized by variable disease activity, with late gestation and the postpartum period representing clinically relevant periods of vulnerability to maternal exacerbations and neonatal involvement. Increased third-trimester MG-ADL scores, particularly among antibody-positive mothers, were associated with TNMG and postpartum exacerbations, supporting close monitoring during these periods.

items.title: A Novel Sequential Regimen of Efgartigimod and Telitacicept as Fast-Acting Treatment for Impeding Crisis of MuSK-MG.
items.authors: Tianjiao Duan, Song Ouyang, Wei Lu, Weifan Yin
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction. The muscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibody-positive subtype often involves bulbar and respiratory muscles, conferring a high risk of myasthenic crisis. We report a very late-onset MuSK-MG case complicated by lung infection and acute heart failure, with a history of peptic ulcer. The patient was sequentially treated with efgartigimod and telitacicept, achieving minimal symptom expression (MSE) within 1.5 months. Following the first efgartigimod infusion, QMG and MG-ADL scores improved from 31 to 23 and 22 to 12, respectively. After five injections of telitacicept, symptoms resolved completely on day 47, with scores further reducing to 2 (QMG) and 0 (MG-ADL). Treatment also reduced IgG levels and MuSK-Ab titers, while IgM remained stable. This case demonstrates the successful sequential use of efgartigimod and telitacicept in managing complicated, late-onset MuSK-MG in a state of impeding crisis.

items.title: Co-Occurrence of Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy and Myasthenia Gravis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
items.authors: Pricilla Yani Gunawan, Jeremiah Hilkiah Wijaya
items.abstract: Co-occurrence of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) and myasthenia gravis (MG) is rare but clinically critical, as treatable MG symptoms may be misattributed to FSHD progression. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively characterize patients with both conditions and to quantitatively synthesize the available individual patient data. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched four databases until 3 April 2026 for original reports providing individual-patient data on confirmed FSHD and MG co-occurrence. We performed descriptive and quantitative syntheses of clinical, genetic, and therapeutic variables. Nine studies were systematically reviewed, with 29 patients contributing to on. FSHD onset significantly preceded MG onset, with a pooled mean interval of 24.21 years. The pooled mean age at MG onset was 62.62 years. All tested patients were acetylcholine receptor antibody positive. MG frequently presented with ocular and bulbar manifestations. Crucially, the pooled estimate for clinical improvement following standard MG-directed therapies was 89.7%. MG in FSHD patients typically emerges late in adulthood as an antibody-positive autoimmune synaptopathy. Recognizing new ocular or bulbar weakness as superimposed MG is essential, providing a highly treatable avenue to reverse functional decline in patients with established myopathy.

items.title: Real-World Clinical Outcomes and Corticosteroid Tapering in Telitacicept-Based Therapy for Ocular Myasthenia Gravis: An Exploratory Analysis by Prior Treatment History.
items.authors: Ran Guo, Chunrong Li, Manman Zhang, Yifan Cheng, Wenting Guo, Bo Jin
items.abstract: Ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) is an autoantibody-mediated disease characterized by extraocular muscle weakness. Telitacicept has shown potential in treating autoimmune diseases, but its efficacy and corticosteroid-tapering outcomes in OMG remain unexamined. This retrospective, multicenter study evaluated the efficacy and corticosteroid-tapering outcomes of telitacicept in 19 OMG patients (11 with refractory OMG and eight with newly/reinitiated treatment OMG). The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving minimal symptom expression (MSE) within 6 months. Secondary endpoints included changes in Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) scores and reductions in daily prednisone dosage, cumulative response rate (CRR), and short-term tolerability. Following 6 months of telitacicept treatment, 68.42% of the overall cohort achieved MSE, with the median MG-ADL score significantly decreasing from 3.00 to 0.00 (p < 0.0001). Daily prednisone dosage substantially decreased: the median daily prednisone dose fell from 20.00 to 5.00 mg (p < 0.0001), and 84.21% of patients received prednisone at ≤5 mg/day at month 6. All patients met the predefined initial response criterion within 5 weeks. The refractory and newly/reinitiated treatment groups achieved final MSE rates of 72.7% and 62.5%, respectively, and both groups showed significant reductions in prednisone dependence. This cohort had no serious adverse events. In this exploratory cohort, telitacicept-based therapy may represent a promising option for OMG, with favorable clinical outcomes, substantial prednisone dose reduction, and acceptable short-term tolerability in patients with different prior treatment histories. Further prospective controlled studies are warranted.

items.title: Potential association between Epstein-Barr virus infection and myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Nana Zhang, Xue Lin, Hongxi Chen, Rui Wang, Xiaofei Wang, Ziyan Shi
items.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) has been implicated in multiple autoimmune disorders; however, its role in myasthenia gravis (MG) remains incompletely defined. We investigated EBV nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA-1)-specific humoral immunity in MG and examined whether human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genotypes modulate this association. Serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels were measured in 106 treatment-naïve MG patients and 230 healthy controls (HCs). An independent MG cohort (n = 244) underwent whole-genome sequencing for HLA genotyping, with 44 treatment-naïve patients also tested for anti-EBNA-1 IgG. MG patients showed higher proportions of anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels above the upper detection limit (>600 U/mL) compared with age- and sex-matched HCs (67% vs. 50%, p = 0.082). Among individuals with detectable antibody levels (3-600 U/mL), MG patients exhibited significantly higher titers than matched HCs (306.0 [181.5-391.0] vs. 157.0 [92.4-250.0] U/mL, p = 0.0065). No significant associations were found between anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels and MG clinical phenotypes. HLA association analyses identified the HLA-DRB4*01:03 - /DRB3*02:02 + genotype as a significant genetic risk factor for generalized MG versus ocular MG (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.29-5.21, p = 0.01). Among patients who were tested for both HLA and anti-EBNA-1 IgG and had anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels >600 U/mL, ocular MG patients carried HLA DRB4*01:03 more frequently than generalized MG patients (81.8% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.006). Our findings suggest a potential association between EBV-specific immune responses and MG. Furthermore, the HLA-DRB4*01:03-/DRB3*02:02+ genotype may confer susceptibility to generalized MG, supporting an interaction between EBV infection and host genetics in MG pathogenesis.

items.title: Infections and the neuromuscular junction: From direct neurotoxicity to immune-mediated dysfunction.
items.authors: Christian Messina, Annarita Botta, Silvia Mascolo, Roberto Parrella
items.abstract: Infectious diseases and disorders of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) are linked by complex and heterogeneous mechanisms that extend beyond direct pathogen-mediated injury. While some infectious agents can directly impair neuromuscular transmission, others may act as triggers of autoimmunity or contribute to the exacerbation of pre-existing NMJ disorders. However, the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain incompletely understood. In this narrative review, we summarize the current evidence regarding infections associated with NMJ dysfunction. Available evidence suggests that infections may influence NMJ disorders through multiple pathways, including direct neurotoxicity, immune dysregulation, molecular mimicry, and loss of immune tolerance. While some pathogens have been more consistently associated with NMJ dysfunction, for many others the available evidence remains limited to isolated reports, preventing definitive conclusions regarding causality. Overall, infections represent important contributors to the spectrum of NMJ disorders, acting as direct disruptors of neuromuscular transmission, autoimmune triggers, or disease modifiers. A better understanding of pathogen-host interactions at the NMJ may provide new insights into disease mechanisms and potentially identify novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Future prospective studies integrating clinical, neurophysiological, and immunological approaches are needed to clarify the role of infectious agents in NMJ pathophysiology.

items.title: Immune remodeling after thymectomy in patients with anti-AChR antibodies.
items.authors: Naoshi Koizumi, Makoto Kinoshita, Yoshiaki Yasumizu, Tomohiro Yata, Daisuke Motooka, Ryohei Yamamura
items.abstract: Thymectomy is an established treatment for thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis (MG). However, a subset of patients develop new-onset MG after surgery. Although thymectomy affects immune homeostasis, its comprehensive impact on the peripheral immune system remains unclear, particularly at the single-cell transcriptomic level. Therefore, we aimed to characterize immune remodeling following thymectomy in anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive patients without overt MG. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from three anti-AChR antibody-positive patients before and 7-22 months after thymectomy. Single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing were subsequently performed. Cell populations were annotated using SingleR and Azimuth. Differential gene expression was analyzed, followed by gene set enrichment analysis. TCR repertoire diversity was assessed using scRepertoire. Additionally, cell-cell communication was inferred using CellChat. Thymectomy induced broad immune remodeling characterized by a relative reduction in naïve CD4 + and CD8 + T cells and a concomitant relative increase in natural killer (NK) cells, particularly the CD56 dim subset. Despite the relative decline in naïve T cells, activation-associated genes were upregulated and inflammatory pathways were enriched in the remaining cells, indicating an activation-associated transcriptional state. Monocyte subsets showed marked transcriptional changes, including upregulation of the expression of immediate early genes and downregulation of that of antigen presentation-related and inflammatory genes, consistent with substantial transcriptional remodeling. Furthermore, cell-cell communication analysis revealed a qualitative shift in the dominant signaling axis after thymectomy. Pre-thymectomy networks were characterized by TNF- and resistin-mediated signaling, whereas post-thymectomy networks were dominated by IFNγ signaling, primarily originating from CD56 dim NK cells and targeting monocyte subsets. Thymectomy induces coordinated remodeling of the peripheral immune system, which involves reduced thymic output, activation-associated transcriptional changes in T cells, relative increase in the proportion of NK cells, and transcriptional remodeling of monocytes. The dominant inflammatory signaling axis shifts from TNF/resistin-centered to IFNγ-centered communication after thymectomy. This bidirectional immune modulation may underlie both therapeutic effects and susceptibility to post-thymectomy MG, highlighting the importance of intercellular signaling dynamics in maintaining immune homeostasis.

items.title: Case Report: Fulminant meningococcus-meningitis under treatment with ravulizumab despite complete vaccination-a rare but severe complication.
items.authors: Gábor Kozák, Stefan Förster, Michael Haap, Reimer Riessen, Samuel Böhm-Gonzalez, Jan-Hendrik Stahl
items.abstract: Complement C5 inhibitors such as ravulizumab are increasingly used for acetylcholine receptor-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (MG) but confer a relevant risk of invasive meningococcal infection. We report a rare case of fulminant meningococcal meningitis despite complete vaccination, highlighting the limits of current preventive strategies. Case report. A 41-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor-positive MG was treated with ravulizumab after two-dose series meningococcal vaccination (MenACWY and MenB). One month after therapy initiation, she presented with nausea, vomiting and rapidly developed impaired consciousness. CSF showed neutrophilic pleocytosis, hypoglycorrhachia, and high lactate, consistent with bacterial meningitis. Rapid testing and culture confirmed Neisseria meningitidis serotype Y . Despite immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics, neurological deterioration required intubation and intensive care. The patient recovered after 18 days of intravenous antibiotics and was switched from ravulizumab to rozanolixizumab. This case illustrates that vaccination does not abolish the risk of fulminant meningococcal infection under complement inhibition. Awareness, patient information, and rapid initiation of antibiotics are critical. Clinicians should counsel patients and relatives that meningitis may occur despite vaccination and promote early recognition strategies.

items.title: Good's syndrome and infections in a large retrospective cohort of thymoma.
items.authors: Wenji Jia, Lei Jin, Xiao Huan, Chong Yan, Jianying Xi, Liewen Pang, Chongbo Zhao, Jie Song, Xianglin Chu, Sushan Luo
items.abstract: Good's syndrome (GS) is an immunodeficiency associated with thymoma characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia. The co-existence of recurrent infections may be associated with quality of life and overall survival. Despite its relevance, the impact of GS on patients with thymoma has rarely been studied in large cohorts. This is a retrospective cohort study of patients with pathologically confirmed thymoma recruited between May 2010 and November 2024. Data on peripheral immune profile, infections, and paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS) were collected and analyzed. Of 1001 patients with thymoma, we ultimately included 158 patients who underwent peripheral immune profiling. The prevalence of GS was 45.6% (72/158), and the infections were reported in 43.69% (69/158). Infection rates were higher in the GS group than in non-GS group (50% versus 32.72%, P = 0.0384). Among the 121 pathogens identified from this cohort, bacteria were the most prevalent (52.07%, 63/121), followed by fungi (34.71%, 42/121) and virus (13.22%, 16/121). Patients with infections had significantly lower overall survival compared with those without infections (P < 0.001). In addition, patients with multiple PNS had poorer survival than those with a single PNS (P < 0.001). No significant difference in overall survival was found between the GS and the non-GS groups. GS and infections are prevalent in patients with thymoma. Infections and multiple PNS were associated with poorer survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and intervention for improving prognosis and long-term survival in patients with thymoma.
